candidate.blueprint_locator: Appendix A, Basic Care and Comfort > Assistive Devices, printed p.36 / PDF p.40; related activity statement: assist client to compensate for a physical or sensory impairment using assistive devices/positioning
candidate.blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — Assistive Devices / safe mobility and transfer
candidate.educational_objective: Use mechanical patient-handling devices to reduce hazardous manual lifting while safely assisting with transfers and repositioning.

options.A: It reduces the need for hazardous manual lifting during patient-handling tasks
options.B: It eliminates the need to assess the client's transfer ability before each use
options.C: It is intended only for clients with bariatric body size
options.D: It allows transfers to be completed without trained staff participation

candidate.rationale: NIOSH identifies manual lifting, moving, and repositioning of patients as a major risk for work-related musculoskeletal injury and recommends safe patient-handling technology, including assistive lifting devices, to reduce injury and strain. Therefore A is the best answer. Mechanical lifts do not eliminate the need to assess the client, are not limited to bariatric clients, and still require appropriate trained staff use.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Safe patient-handling and mobility technology uses assistive lifting devices to reduce injury and strain associated with manual patient lifting, moving, and repositioning.
candidate.source_document_title: About Safe Patient Handling and Mobility
candidate.source_locator: Overview and 'Prevention steps and strategies': patient handling includes manual lifting/moving/repositioning; assistive lifting devices and SPHM technology reduce healthcare-worker injury and strain and support safe patient handling
candidate.source_organization: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH), Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
candidate.stem: A nurse uses a ceiling-mounted mechanical lift when transferring a client. What is the primary safety benefit of this device?
